University, Graduate School, & Departmental Opportunities
At Rutgers Graduate School-Camden, we consider your academic journey and the ways you contribute to our campus community. In return, we offer a variety of financial aid options tailored to your needs and potential. This section highlights the funding opportunities available to graduate students at Rutgers University, including scholarships, assistantships, and fellowships from the Graduate School and various departments. Unless otherwise specified, applying for these university, graduate school, and departmental opportunities requires submitting the strongest possible application, with no additional steps. Early applications are generally given preference.
In the following discussion, Assistant Deans Erick Watt-Udogu and Danielle Askew will guide you through the available funding options.
TEACHING AND GRADUATE ASSISTANTSHIPS
The department’s admissions committee and graduate program director award Teaching and Graduate Assistantships to exceptional full-time applicants. These positions come with significant benefits, including full tuition and fee remission, a generous stipend, and health benefits. The programs offering these assistantships are:
Childhood Studies – PhD
Computational and Integrative Biology – PhD
Creative Writing – MFA
Public Affairs – PhD
Prevention Science – PhD
MASTER’S MERIT SCHOLARSHIPS
These scholarships are available to high-achieving students enrolled in our graduate programs. Qualified full-time students have the opportunity to receive scholarships covering up to 50% of in-state tuition. To be eligible, students must be registered for at least six credits.
GRADUATE SCHOOL OUT-OF-STATE MERIT SCHOLARSHIP
The scholarship is competitively awarded to incoming domestic master’s applicants who reside outside of New Jersey. It covers the difference in tuition costs between in-state and out-of-state rates for full-time students taking a minimum of 9 credits, up to 12 credits per semester. The scholarship is renewable for up to 4 consecutive semesters, covering 2 academic years, specifically the fall and spring semesters.
INTERNATIONAL CHANCELLOR’S SCHOLARSHIPS
The Graduate School International Chancellor’s Scholarships are available to all non-sponsored, international F-1 applicants who meet the requirements and enroll full-time in a master’s in the Graduate School. These scholarships are awarded based on the merit of the candidate.
RUTGERS UNIVERSITY-WIDE FELLOWSHIPS
Graduate Program Directors nominate exceptional candidates from the fall applicant pool for University Fellowships.
Bunche Fellowship
Two Bunche Fellowships will be awarded to two incoming, full-time graduate students representing a diversity population. The fellowship includes a stipend plus tuition remission with a possible reappointment for a second year.
Hazel Vera Dean Fellowship
The Hazel Vera Dean fellowship is a scholarship awarded to one graduate student who is a resident of New Jersey and shows financial need.
Trustee Fellowship in the Humanities and Social Sciences
One Trustee Fellowship will be awarded to a student representing a diversity population and pursuing a master’s degree likely to lead to a Ph.D. in the same field. The fellowship includes a stipend and tuition remission with a possible reappointment for a second year.
Presidential Fellowship
Presidential Fellowships are university wide fellowships for PhD applicants that are awarded to an incoming graduate student in a doctoral program selected for a TA/GA . Exceptional candidates are nominated by their Program Director for consideration.
GRADUATE DEPARTMENTAL SCHOLARSHIPS
History (M.A.)
The History Fellowship provides exceptional students with a stipend and tuition remission. The Graduate Program Committee evaluates and selects applicants for this funding.
Psychology (M.A.)
The Psychology Fellowship provides exceptional students with tuition remission. The Graduate Program Committee evaluates and selects applicants for this funding.
Public Administration (M.P.A.)
Coverdell Fellowship: If you are a Returning Peace Corps Volunteer (RPCV), please visit the Department of Public Policy and Administration site for more information.
Federal & State Funding Opportunities for Domestic Students
To apply for Federal and state financial aid programs, completing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is a crucial step in securing financial aid for your graduate studies. The FAFSA is a form provided by the U.S. Department of Education that determines your eligibility for federal student aid, including grants, loans, and work-study programs for domestic students.
The Graduate Federal Work-Study program is an exclusive financial aid option available to domestic graduate students. It is awarded based on financial need, as assessed by the FAFSA. Eligible students may receive up to $2,000 in work-study funds for the academic year. Participants in the program typically work 5-7 hours per week, contributing to their department or a campus office. Work-study positions encompass a wide range of roles, including research, administration, and assisting faculty.
Please note: If you are an international student, the FAFSA and Federal Work Study are not applicable.
To navigate the FAFSA application process, consider these tips:
FAFSA Website
Start by visiting the Federal Student Aid website. This is where you can access the application form and other important resources.
Rutgers School Code
The Rutgers University school code is 002629.
Application Period
Start by visiting the Federal Student Aid website. This is where you can access the application form and other important resources.
For more detailed information and to access the FAFSA application (for domestic students), visit: fafsa.ed.gov.
Financing Options for International Graduate Students
International students looking to fund their graduate education can explore the following resources. These loan providers operate independently and manage their own application and approval processes.
These options are shared as potential resources. Students are responsible for reviewing terms and determining whether these or other financing options meet their needs.
Prodigy Finance provides loans to international students in many Rutgers–Camden graduate programs. Program eligibility varies and can be confirmed on their website.
🔗 Check eligible programs through Prodigy Finance
MPOWER offers loans to international and DACA students enrolled in graduate programs at Rutgers–Camden. All graduate programs are currently eligible.
🔗 Learn more about MPOWER Financing
